scope: Align the existing Telegram E2E busy-owner-DM scenario with the current live-steering behavior; test fixture only, no production change.
sourceBaseDescription: Merged trunk ddd4cbcfa plus native Ollama provider repairs; this is not a pure-trunk baseline.

before.outcome: FAIL: timed out waiting for chat 5555 eventually gets the real answer for message #2
before.location: test/channels.telegram.e2e.test.js:314 (waitUntil), caller :633 in the pre-change fixture
before.cause: The fixture held the first model completion indefinitely and assumed a second plain owner DM would cancel it. Current production correctly adds that DM to the same active run; the fixture never released its own gate.
before.candidateComparison: git diff ddd4cbcfa..9f7ab4b4c was empty for sidecar/channels/hub.js, sidecar/channels/telegram.js, sidecar/loop.js and test/channels.telegram.e2e.test.js.

after.responseDiscriminator: Only a provider request containing the actual system steering note produces Follow-up applied: TELEGRAM_FOLLOWUP_APPLIED; neither the acknowledgement nor the initial generic answer satisfies delivery.
after.fixtureGate: Matches the exact original user message, so unrelated auxiliary completions cannot consume the gate.

cases: L: transient workspace-mutex retry delivers a real answer
L2: bounded retry exhaustion returns an honest busy reply
L3-L4: other errors are not retried and newer messages can supersede a retry
X: same-run steering and refused-steer fallback behavior

verification: After runner exit, no node.exe command line containing this provider-triage-1011 worktree remained.
limitations: Actual local sidecar, synthetic loopback Telegram and OpenRouter fixtures; no external provider or real Telegram account used.
